turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Ned? Straight through, doctor's free. Second door on the left.
[SEG0002] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ta. Come on, shoes off.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): G'day, I'm Dr Singh. Sit wherever you like. What's brought you in today?
[SEG0004] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): These dry itchy patches. Behind his knees and in the elbow creases. He's four and he's been scratching something awful.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): You poor thing. Ned, does it itch?
[SEG0006] person_4 (PATIENT): Yeah.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Which bit is the worst?
[SEG0008] person_4 (PATIENT): Knees.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): When does the scratching really get going?
[SEG0010] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): At night. He wakes up scratching. It's better in the day.
[SEG0011] person_4 (PATIENT): Night.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long has this been going on for?
[SEG0013] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Umm, about four months. I nearly said since June, after winter, but nah, it's about four months.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any weeping or pus in the skin? Any fever?
[SEG0015] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No weeping. No fever.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Aside from the skin, how's his breathing, tummy, wee and poo?
[SEG0017] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): All fine. No wheeze. Eats like a horse. He talked footy the whole way here, drove me mad.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ha, love that. What creams have you got on the go?

[SEG0019] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Big white tub, thick cream, morning and night. Pink tube once a day on the angry bits. Chemist said the pink one's a steroid. The label's rubbed off though, I think it might be hydrocortazone oh point five, but err don't quote me.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): And does the pink one help him?
[SEG0021] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): A bit, yeah. Sometimes it stings.
[SEG0022] person_4 (PATIENT): Stings.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines or creams?
[SEG0024] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. None.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any asthma or eczema in the family?
[SEG0026] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His dad's got asthma. Been on a puffer for years. No eczema in the family.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Has a doctor given Ned's rash a name before?

[SEG0028] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): GP last year reckoned it looked like eczema. They did a blood test and said it was borderline. I never got the actual number, and I can't remember the month. Just sometime last year.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll have a look, mate. Dry thickened patches behind both knees and in both elbow creases, and a few scratch marks. No break in the skin and no weeping.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Plan for now, keep the white tub morning and night, and we'll bump that pink steroid to twice a day for a fortnight. See how we go.
[SEG0031] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Well, actually, it stings him, and we can't read the tube. It's nearly empty too. And that blood test, he screamed the place down, I don't want another one today.

[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yep, that changes things. Forget the twice a day idea, and stop the pink tube, I'm not happy using an unnamed steroid that stings. I'll start Advantan fatty ointment, methylprednisolone aceponate 0.1 percent, a thin layer once a day on the rough patches for seven days, then stop. You can keep the white cream, and please get QV cream and use it four times a day when the skin looks dry.

[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Looks like an eczema flare to me, not an infection. The nurse takes allergy bloods Thursday morning, no fasting, a normal brekkie is fine. I'll see you in two weeks. If those bloods are borderline we do skin prick testing, and if it hasn't settled by the review we'll swab the skin.

spec.situation: Mother brings a child with itchy dry patches behind the knees and elbows, worse at night, scratching; creams named by colour; father has asthma; doctor adjusts steroid cream and moisturiser advice.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
